title: Cajun Lime Shrimp & Black Bean Bowls
displayTitle: Cajun Lime Shrimp & Black Bean Bowls
seoTitle: Cajun Lime Shrimp & Black Bean Bowls | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Cajun-seared shrimp with black beans, corn, and rice in a bright lime dressing
subtitle: Cajun-seared shrimp with black beans, corn, and rice in a bright lime dressing
description: Shrimp gets a quick Cajun sear, then joins black beans, charred corn, and rice with a lime dressing. It cooks fast enough for a busy shift and gives crews a lean seafood option beyond salmon and cod.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.instruction: Rinse rice, bring it with water to a boil in a lidded pot, then reduce to low and simmer 18 minutes. Rest 10 minutes, then fluff.

steps.title: Warm the beans and char the corn
steps.instruction: Warm black beans in a saucepan with a splash of water. In a separate dry skillet, toast corn over medium-high 4–5 minutes until a few kernels brown. Combine with diced bell pepper.

steps.title: Season the shrimp
steps.instruction: Pat shrimp dry and toss with cajun seasoning until evenly coated. Dry shrimp sears better than wet shrimp.

steps.title: Sear the shrimp
steps.instruction: Heat oil in a wide skillet over medium-high until shimmering. Sear shrimp in a single layer, 90 seconds per side, until pink, opaque, and lightly charred at the edges. Do not overcrowd or overcook — shrimp turns rubbery fast.

steps.title: Mix the lime dressing
steps.instruction: Whisk lime juice, olive oil, and a pinch of salt. Toss half with the bean and corn mixture and reserve the rest for drizzling.

steps.title: Build the bowls
steps.instruction: Layer rice, black beans, and corn-pepper mix in each bowl, top with seared shrimp, and finish with the remaining lime dressing and cilantro if using.

proTips: Prep tip: Pat shrimp completely dry before seasoning so it sears instead of steams.
Rookie tip: Pull shrimp the moment it turns pink and opaque — a few extra seconds turns it tough.
Cook shrimp in batches rather than crowding the pan for real color and char.
Swap shrimp for chicken or tofu using the same seasoning and timing adjustments.
tonightSpread: Main: Cajun lime shrimp and black bean bowls
Sides: Tortilla chips, extra lime wedges
Set hot components closest to the crew; cold crunch and toppings at the far end of the line.
Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a run.
leftovers: Store shrimp separately from rice and beans; reheat gently in a skillet just until warm.
Cool rice and beans in shallow containers within two hours of cooking.
Shrimp is best eaten within 2 days — it toughens more than other proteins on repeated reheats.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Shrimp cooks in minutes, so this comes together fast on a night the hall doesn't have a lot of prep time, and the beans and rice keep it filling despite the lean protein.
mealPrepNotes: Make-ahead: rice, beans, and corn all hold well up to 4 days. Storage: keep shrimp separate and reheat gently — it toughens fast if overcooked a second time. Reheating: warm shrimp briefly in a skillet just until hot, not longer.
substitutions: Use chicken breast instead of shrimp.
Use tofu for a vegetarian version with the same seasoning.
Use brown rice instead of jasmine rice.
